rationale: The entry’s core—that Night is the absence of Day/Light, with Light as open/visible obedience (righteous deeds that can be seen), and is therefore the sphere of concealed evil deeds, sleep, and the opposite of Day—is carried better by the supplied dualism (Gen 1:5 naming; 1 Thess 5:5–7 children of day vs night who sleep and are drunken; chapter’s chain from law/word as light, Matt 5 good works as shining light, John 3 evil deeds hiding from light, Rom 13 works of darkness) than by a looser ‘spiritual darkness’ label. That core is the same referent as the mainstream reading, only more mechanically precise. The printed large-scale claim (night as the entire interval from the fall until the Kingdom begins on earth) is a material glossary assertion that the cited texts and chapter do not establish: night is named in the good creation before the fall, and the eschatological ‘night far spent’ texts mark the present age awaiting day, not a fall-to-kingdom span. Hence PERSUADED on core, CORE_ONLY overall.
book_core_identification: Night is the absence of Day and Light, where Light is visible/open obedience (righteous conduct that can be seen), and is therefore the opposite of Day.
book_secondary_elaborations: marked by sleep or death and by sinful deeds concealed in darkness
At the largest scale, it is the period from the fall of man until the Kingdom of God begins on earth
unsupported_glossary_assertions: At the largest scale, it is the period from the fall of man until the Kingdom of God begins on earth
chapter_only_objections: Light reduced strictly to the law lived as visible good works (and oil/tried obedience) as the sole content of the symbol
Counterfeit light as self-kindled sparks / fig-leaf covering
Ninth-plague Egypt/Israel staging as the map of the dualism
Outer-darkness / wedding-garment / foolish-virgins merger as the single end-state of those without light
John 9:4 and John 11:10 / 12:35 pressed as the primary death/end-of-work and stumbling mechanics for night
strongest_counter_interpretation: In figurative Christian use, night primarily symbolizes spiritual and moral darkness—sin, evil, unbelief, ignorance of God, and separation from divine light—contrasted with day/light as God, Christ, truth, and salvation; it is multivalent (present evil age awaiting the Day of the Lord; season of trial; end of opportunity; occasionally positive setting for prayer/revelation) and many occurrences are simply literal time markers.
counter_core_identification: Night is spiritual/moral darkness (sin, evil, unbelief, separation from God’s light), the contrasting counterpart to day/light.
material_core_denial: None; the mainstream ‘spiritual darkness / works of darkness’ reading describes the same referent as absence of visible obedience/open righteousness and does not require denying that night is the opposite of day/light.
counter_case: Rom 13:12, 1 Thess 5:4–8, Eph 5:8–11, John 3:19–21, John 13:30, Rev 21:25 / 22:5 are classically read as moral/eschatological darkness vs light without needing Light = visible obedience as the definitional content
Gen 1:5 is first a creation naming of physical darkness; moral dualism is a later application, not proof that night’s large-scale meaning begins at the fall
Sleep in 1 Thess 5 is unwatchfulness of ‘others,’ not a definitional mark that night = sleep or death
Positive or neutral night uses (rest, protection, revelation, literal chronology) show the term is not exhausted by ‘absence of visible obedience’
book_explanatory_advantages: Unifies law/word-as-light, Matt 5 shining good works, and John 3 concealment-of-evil-deeds into one mechanical opposite of night
Makes 1 Thess 5:5–7 (children of day vs night who sleep and are drunken) and Rom 13 cast-off-works-of-darkness a direct consequence of the same light definition
Keeps Day/Night as the Gen 1:5 named pair rather than a free-floating metaphor
counter_explanatory_advantages: Covers the full multivalence (eschatological age, trial/weeping night, death/opportunity, literal time, occasional positive night) without forcing every use through ‘visible obedience’
Does not require starting symbolic night at the fall when Gen 1 already names Night in the good creation
Matches the broad settled consensus without extra symbolic system premises
decisive_sources: Genesis 1:5 (light called Day, darkness called Night)
1 Thessalonians 5:5–7 (children of light/day vs night/darkness; sleep and drunkenness in the night)
Chapter chain: law/word as light; Matt 5 good works as light men see; John 3 evil deeds loving darkness to avoid reproof; Rom 13 night far spent / works of darkness vs armour of light
unresolved_objections: Whether ‘death’ is a definitional mark of night on the same footing as sleep and concealed deeds, or only a homiletic extension of John 9:4
How far the creation naming of Night can be stretched into a moral age that begins only at the fall
